## Purpose and scope

This handoff supports the planned rewrite of Chapter 17's scientific-values
word-search activity. It records the source, tested word families, thematic
groups, and an activity progression. It does not edit Chapter 17, regenerate the
corpus, render the book, or publish anything.

**Recommendation:** use the carefulness family as the main worked example,
accuracy as parallel practice, and research credit as a first thematic search.
Offer broader groups as choices or extensions. These are instructional
recommendations, not claims established by the article.

## Verified source and corpus facts

Peels, Rik, Jeroen de Ridder, Tamarinde Haven, and Lex Bouter. (2019).
"Value pluralism in research integrity." *Research Integrity and Peer Review*,
4, Article 18. <https://doi.org/10.1186/s41073-019-0076-4>.

The preparation report, `Science_Values_Creation.Rmd` in this folder, documents
extraction from the publisher's version of record and its
[CC BY 4.0 notice](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s41073-019-0076-4#rightslink).
Retain source credit, license information, and the description of preparation
changes. That report also records an unresolved check of underlying licenses
for attributed quotations from research codes; do not describe that separate
check as completed by this handoff.

The student file is `../data/Science_Values.rds`. It contains a plain character
vector of **197 natural passages**. Paragraphs, list items, notes, references,
and identification records are individual entries; headings attach once to
the next entry. Citation and rights information remain with the text.

All counts below search the complete supplied vector, including references,
notes, headings, and notices. They count **matching passages**, not occurrences
of a word. A passage matching two alternatives counts once in the combined
search. Counts from separate searches must not simply be added.

### Read the existing file without changing it

When knitted from its repository location, the report finds the OER repository
above this folder. The optional `corpus_path` parameter allows an explicit input
for an independent check. No chunk saves or replaces the corpus.

```{r read-existing-corpus}
corpus_override <- if (exists("params")) params$corpus_path else NULL
if (is.null(corpus_override)) {
  input <- knitr::current_input(dir = TRUE)
  start <- if (length(input) == 1L && nzchar(input)) {
    dirname(normalizePath(input, mustWork = TRUE))
  } else getwd()
  repeat {
    candidate <- file.path(start, "chapters", "07-thoroughness", "data", "Science_Values.rds")
    if (file.exists(file.path(start, "_quarto.yml")) && file.exists(candidate)) break
    parent <- dirname(start)
    if (identical(parent, start)) stop("Open the OER project or supply corpus_path.")
    start <- parent
  }
  corpus_file <- normalizePath(candidate, mustWork = TRUE)
} else {
  corpus_file <- normalizePath(corpus_override, mustWork = TRUE)
}
Science_Values <- readRDS(corpus_file)
stopifnot(is.character(Science_Values), is.null(attributes(Science_Values)),
          length(Science_Values) == 197L, all(!is.na(Science_Values)))
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  passages = length(Science_Values),
  file_md5 = unname(tools::md5sum(corpus_file))
))
```

## 1. Word families: a manageable starting point

A prefix search finds spelling relatives. It does not infer synonyms or a
passage's meaning. For example, the R string `"\\bcareful"` requires a word
boundary before `careful` and allows following letters, returning *careful*,
*carefully*, and *carefulness*. It needs no wildcard or new package.

The absence of a final `\\b` is deliberate. In contrast,
`"\\bcareful\\b"` finds *careful* without including *carefully* or *carefulness*.
An explicit alternative is `"\\b(careful|carefully|carefulness)\\b"`.

```{r define-word-families}
family_patterns <- c(
  accountability = "\\baccountability\\b",
  accuracy = "\\baccurate",
  carefulness = "\\bcareful",
  thoroughness = "\\bthoroughness\\b",
  openness = "\\bopen",
  transparency = "\\btransparen",
  disclosure = "\\bdisclos",
  honesty = "\\bhonest",
  responsibility = "\\bresponsib",
  conflict = "\\bconflict",
  humility = "\\b(humility|humble)\\b"
)
family_forms <- c(
  "accountability",
  "accurate, accurately",
  "careful, carefully, carefulness",
  "thoroughness",
  "open, open-mindedness, openly, openness",
  "transparency, transparent, transparently",
  "disclose, disclosing, disclosure",
  "honest, honesty",
  "responsible, responsibly, responsibility, responsibilities",
  "conflict, conflicts, conflicting",
  "humility, humble"
)
```

Searches use `stringr::regex(..., ignore_case = TRUE)`. The expected counts record
the checked corpus; a changed result should prompt review rather than an
automatic rewrite of the handoff.

```{r count-word-families}
count_passages <- function(pattern) {
  sum(stringr::str_detect(Science_Values,
                         stringr::regex(pattern, ignore_case = TRUE)))
}
family_counts <- vapply(family_patterns, count_passages, integer(1))
stopifnot(identical(unname(family_counts), c(5L, 4L, 5L, 2L, 14L, 11L, 7L, 8L, 23L, 22L, 3L)))
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  search = names(family_patterns),
  forms_found = family_forms,
  matching_passages = unname(family_counts)
), row.names = FALSE)
```

**Instructional judgment:** the accuracy and carefulness families produce small,
useful sets. The broad responsibility and conflict searches suit optional
exploration. Accountability has five hits, but three are values lists and two
are the journal title *Accountability in Research* in reference entries. It is
a valid counting exercise, not five explanatory discussions of accountability.

## 2. Connections: combine related concepts into themes

The following groups connect different concepts. They are not synonym lists,
and some terms reasonably belong to more than one group. Disclosure connects
openness and honest reporting, but it also appears where information must be
protected. Plagiarism names a violation rather than a virtue.

Keep *carefulness* and *accuracy* distinct even when searching them together.
Similarly, transparency and honesty can support reproducibility without being
equivalent to reproducibility. No added term is claimed to cover an absent
course value such as tenacity or courage.

```{r define-themed-searches}
theme_terms <- list(
  careful_inquiry = c("accurate", "accurately", "careful", "carefully",
                     "carefulness", "thoroughness"),
  open_research = c("open", "open-mindedness", "openly", "openness",
                    "transparency", "transparent", "transparently",
                    "disclose", "disclosing", "disclosure", "sharing"),
  honest_reporting = c("honest", "honesty", "disclose", "disclosing", "disclosure"),
  accountability_and_duties = c("accountability", "responsible", "responsibly",
                              "responsibility", "responsibilities", "duty", "duties"),
  research_credit = c("authorship", "ownership", "plagiarism", "acknowledgement"),
  working_together = c("collaboration", "communication"),
  protecting_people = c("privacy", "confidentiality", "consent", "autonomy"),
  competing_values = c("conflict", "conflicts", "conflicting", "humility", "humble",
                       "reasoning", "judgment", "judgments")
)
```

Build one bounded OR pattern for each group, using the alternation already
introduced in Chapter 17. These terms contain no regex punctuation needing
escaping; a hyphen outside a character class is literal. This helper is for
these specified terms, not an unrestricted dictionary parser.

```{r build-themed-patterns}
theme_patterns <- vapply(theme_terms, function(terms) {
  paste0("\\b(", paste(terms, collapse = "|"), ")\\b")
}, character(1))
theme_counts <- vapply(theme_patterns, count_passages, integer(1))
stopifnot(identical(unname(theme_counts), c(10L, 21L, 15L, 28L, 8L, 8L, 11L, 24L)))
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  theme = names(theme_terms),
  terms = vapply(theme_terms, paste, character(1), collapse = ", "),
  matching_passages = unname(theme_counts)
), row.names = FALSE)
```

Use these as a menu, not eight required searches. Aiming for about five matches
works well for the smaller word families. Combining several concepts naturally
returns more passages; students need only interpret one or two selected results.

Caution, rigor, and precision can be optional additions to careful inquiry. The
larger group also including care finds 15 passages, but *care* includes animal
care and one *rigor* hit is a book title. They broaden the topic beyond the
recommended ten-passage starting group.

Collaboration and communication can share an activity with conflict. Start with
their eight-passage group, then search the conflict family separately. Combining
all five terms returns 28 passages. Many conflicts are between research norms,
not disputes between collaborators, so do not label every hit interpersonal.

### Confirm the optional expansions

```{r check-optional-expansions}
expanded_care <- c(theme_terms$careful_inquiry, "care", "caution", "rigor", "precision")
collaboration_conflict <- c(theme_terms$working_together, "conflict", "conflicts", "conflicting")
bounded_or <- function(terms) paste0("\\b(", paste(terms, collapse = "|"), ")\\b")
stopifnot(count_passages(bounded_or(expanded_care)) == 15L,
          count_passages(bounded_or(collaboration_conflict)) == 28L)
```

## 3. Recommended activity progression

1. **Predict, detect, count, retrieve.** Use the carefulness family. Preserve the
   existing logical-vector, `sum()`, `which()`, and indexing skills. Ask students
   to distinguish five matching passages from the total number of occurrences.
2. **Compare exact and family searches.** Compare whole-word *careful* (2) with
   the careful family (5). Try whole-word *accurate* (3) and its family (4).
   Explain why the pattern's final boundary changes the result.
3. **Build a connection.** Combine authorship, ownership, plagiarism, and
   acknowledgement with `|` (8 passages). This introduces a deliberately chosen
   theme rather than just a shared spelling.
4. **Choose a theme and make an index.** Offer the table as a menu. Use readable
   theme names as index names and store their regex patterns separately. The
   existing `lapply()`, `which()`, and indexing approach still applies.
5. **Interpret one or two results.** Ask: "Which retrieved passage best explains
   your theme, and which match needs more context?" A keyword match identifies a
   candidate passage; it does not establish the passage's position or meaning.
6. **Optional comparison.** Compare openness with protection of people, or
   examine the conflict family alongside humility. This reaches the article's
   central argument about values that pull in different directions.

The original exact *carefulness* search (2 passages) is also a good short preview.
Its two matches are substantive discussions, even though the larger family is
better for demonstrating expansion.

### Verify the proposed exact-versus-family comparison

```{r check-teaching-comparison}
stopifnot(count_passages("\\bcareful\\b") == 2L,
          count_passages("\\baccurate\\b") == 3L,
          count_passages("\\bcarefulness\\b") == 2L)
```

## 4. Meaning checks and useful passage anchors

These anchors identify useful locations in the current 197-passage file. Their
descriptions are instructional judgments based on reading the retrieved text;
numbers may change after a future extraction.

| Passage | Why it is useful |
|---|---|
| 47 | Connects values, norms, virtues, reporting limitations, carefulness, thoroughness, and open-mindedness. |
| 95 | Uses possible equipment or programming problems to explore novelty versus carefulness in deciding whether to publish. |
| 103 | States a concise tension between openness/transparency and privacy. |
| 113 | Develops intellectual humility, listening, and considering other reasonable viewpoints. |

Important interpretation prompts for the editor:

- The open family includes mental open-mindedness, information sharing, and
  *Open Access* in the rights notice. These are related spellings with different
  meanings. A word boundary treats a hyphen as a boundary, so even
  `"\\bopen\\b"` matches the *open* part of *open-mindedness*.
- Disclosure searches include *non-disclosure*. Privacy searches include
  arguments for withholding information, and *consent* also appears in two
  "Not applicable" declarations. Read context before assigning a thematic code.
- Ownership also occurs in a privacy/openness discussion. The credit group is
  a useful connection to investigate, not a guarantee that all eight results
  discuss authorship credit in the same way.
- A humility family search finds three passages despite only one literal
  *humility* passage. Autonomy remains a meaningful one-passage search, not a
  synonym for openness or intellectual independence in every context.
- Searching all entries means a single word can be found wherever it occurs.
  Small passage size does not prevent finding it. A zero means the requested
  pattern is absent, not that the whole article was overlooked.

## 5. Scope for the OER editor

The editor should update the Chapter 17 corpus identification from Resnik and
Elliott to Peels and colleagues and add the proper source citation. Retain the
existing RDS download and `Science_Values <- readRDS("Science_Values.rds")` import.
Use *passages* consistently instead of treating entries as pages or sentences.

Revise the corpus examples and practice around the selected families/themes.
Use `Science_Values` consistently where the current practice also says
`Science_vec`. Specify case sensitivity, boundary rules, and whether an exercise
counts passages or occurrences. Replace the current assumption that exact
*bias* and *reproducibility* must match; those whole-word searches are zero in
this text. Related words are not automatically interchangeable concepts.

Check all proposed activity code against the saved corpus, including zero-result
handling and overlap between terms. Keep the actual regex visible to students
when an exact search changes into a family or thematic search. Do not add
automatic stemming or a new text-analysis package for this plan.

This handoff does not authorize unrelated chapter changes or publication. Keep
the preparation report's outstanding source-permission review visible before
public redistribution. Render this internal handoff independently for review,
with output outside the published book, unless publication is separately requested.
